title: Model route microcanvas + compact chart suite for per-route performance
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design and prototype a compact, high-density microcanvas for per-model and per-route performance insights. The goal is a small-multiple chart group that surfaces latency distribution, throughput ribbons, token volume breakdown, and cost decomposition in a space-efficient panel that can be embedded in route and model pages. This ticket covers: detailed chart specs, interaction patterns, data schema expectations for the runtime team, and a Figma prototype for engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with at least three responsive states (narrow sidebar, mid-width panel, full canvas)
Chart spec doc listing metrics, required aggregates (p50/p90/p99), series naming, and sampling cadence
Interaction spec: hover/detail flyout, time-range pinning, version filter, and sticky tooltip implementation
Developer-ready assets: exportable SVGs, color tokens, and spacing variables
UX review sign-off from Console PM and Platform Reliability lead
design_decisions: Use small-multiple layout (3 rows x 2 columns) so charts remain readable when embedded in lists and in the route header
Prefer percentile ribbon overlays (p50/p90/p99) over raw density plots to reduce visual noise for long-tail behaviors
Token volume uses compact stacked bars with per-token-size bands (prompt vs completion) to keep trend clarity at narrow widths
Cost decomposition shown as inline microbars with hover breakdown rather than full pie to save vertical space
Default time window = 1h with quick toggles for 6h, 24h, 7d; allow pinning of a custom range for comparison across pages
tradeoffs: Precision vs readability: aggregated percentile ribbons lose per-request spike detail; we add an optional raw-trace toggle for debug mode
Space constraints limit showing every metric at once; prioritized latency, throughput, token volume, and cost. Error-rate drilldown moved to a separate modal
Rendering complexity: continuous streaming of microcharts may be heavy; suggest server-side downsampling and efficient canvas rendering (WebGL fallback)
chart_specs_summary: Six compact charts: 1) Latency percentiles (area ribbon p50/p90/p99) 2) Throughput ribbons (requests/s by route variant) 3) Token volume bands (prompt/completion) 4) Cost-per-token trend (moving average + per-token breakdown) 5) Concurrency heat ribbon (time vs concurrency) 6) Error-rate sparkline (mini area). Each chart must support hover detail, selective series toggles, and exportable CSV of the visible window.
engineer_hand_off_notes: Data schema expected: timestamp, route_id, model_version, request_count, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, cost_usd, latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p90, latency_ms_p99, errors_count
Suggested sampling: 1s raw ingestion with 10s downsampled rollup as default for UI. Retain raw traces for 7d via separate trace store
Provide percentile computation at ingestion or via a pre-aggregator to avoid client-side heavy lifts
